For one simple interior root α, the Bergman projection h(z,w)=z+a+4w/3 requires h(α,α)=0, hence α=−3a/7, β=−4a/7 and eigenvalue λ*=c0−12c1²/(49c2); exactly 7/4<|a|<7/3 gives one interior and one exterior root. Two distinct interior roots give a Vandermonde zero-coefficient system; repeated roots are excluded via derivative projection and divisibility. Both boundary roots are on the essential curve and no extra off-curve spectrum remains. Collinear roots make the boundary-distance minimum (1−3t/7)(4t/7−1), completing the square gives sharp 1/48 at t=49/24. Orthogonal analytic/antianalytic Bergman series give exact normalized norm²=(1−(3t/7)²)^−2+[−log(1−v)−v]/v, v=(7/(4t))², with logarithmic lower and 49/(36 delta_+²) upper asymptotics. A separate exact Fraction computation verified 51 Fourier-mode eigen-equations and high-precision endpoint identities; algebraic multiplicity is not asserted.
